summary: Owner requires the branching-style adaptation direction: start with mainline's pipeline, modify for Ouro, identify missing generic expressions, and return those changes to shared owners. A separate Ouro attention/executor/cache/sampler path is not the deliverable. Independent paper/oracle checks remain reference consumers.

The existing TwoRange attention helper unconditionally RMS-normalizes projected Q and K, while the pinned Ouro source passes both directly to RoPE. Gamma one does not express absence. Adapt LayerAttentionConfig and the existing helper to make that semantic choice explicit; preserve existing caller graphs.

Umbrella integration spec is a draft. The standalone shared-graph spec has fixed data contracts, ten new literal cases, two existing graph comparisons and an alloc-tier artifact count; independent admission precedes implementation. No production integration or generation performance result is implied by this plan.

Pinned native GGUF converter permutes Q/K rows from HF split-half to interleaved, matching pinned llama ROPE_TYPE_NORM. GGUF Ouro descriptor must select Interleaved; native HF descriptor selects SplitHalf with no row permutation. Head-width-two fixtures cannot distinguish these layouts; interop spec adds asymmetric width-four coordinates and wrong-pairing control.

Capture incumbent ordinary dense/routed/Gemma TwoRange graphs before shared builder mutation. Compatibility wrapper comparisons alone share the candidate implementation and cannot detect shared regressions. Immutable baseline artifacts retain every Op/root and f32 constant bits because JSON null loses negative infinity.

Source-backed mathematical comparison for the Ouro dense projection X[B,K]·W[N,K]^T→Y[B,N]. Current Omega rejects BF16 dense tiling by default; the admitted float tile still widens BF16 into F32 fragments. llama.cpp source has a BF16-fragment/F32-accumulator specialization, but the saved Llama TTFT payload does not identify the selected pipeline. The available local llama build cache records GGML_METAL_USE_BF16=OFF but is not tied to the timing payload.

Owner requires a real-model end-to-end run at every implementation checkpoint: load, prefill, cached decode and emitted tokens. Unit or graph checks alone do not close the checkpoint. Performance comparisons retain matched llama input IDs/output budgets, actual generated IDs/counts, latency/resource/error payloads and sample CoV; failed runs are retained before repair and repeat.

Source review before cached oracle execution found the new cached branch in the context-enumeration loop before a truncating log initialization and the ordinary uncached execution loop. Moved cached requests into the execution loop after setup logging so each case takes exactly its selected route and cached payloads survive. Native rebuild and end-to-end request-count checks are required; source correction alone is not runtime evidence.

C6 configured off/on production setup retained default batch_size and ubatch_size 32, below the dense tile floor 160, whereas native llama used 256. Total prefix length 256 and a changed untimed full-prefix diagnostic are not evidence of tiled timed generation. Preserve C6 as its own condition; C7 registers explicit batch/ubatch256, context320 and symmetric request-bracketed dispatch/source capture.

Default and configured off/on cached generation cohorts executed through LoadedModel::generate_from_ids with native llama requests. Independent C6 recount preserves complete trajectories, signed initial diagnostic differences, raw durations and N-1 CoV. Identical emitted trajectories coexist with differing logit coordinates; neither trajectory equality nor this below-floor cohort establishes universal numerical or tiled-performance equivalence.

Serving explicitly rejects parallel_sequences other than one and phase_schedule.prefill_before_decode=false. Existing microbatch prefill loops drain inside one request; they do not schedule multiple active streams. PrefixState already owns per-prefix host KV, but is not a cross-stream packed decode batch. Owner asks to segregate bursty prefill and multiple decode streams in the shared pipeline. Single-request tiled measurements cannot establish scheduling behavior under arrivals.

Strict C7 recount initially failed its fixed rounding bound: JSON parsing changed low bits of recorded f64 durations and uncentered Welford amplified offset rounding. Enable serde_json float_roundtrip on the unchanged locked version and center Welford at the first sample; preserve the bound. Two literal regression cases recover exact source values and reject corrupted statistics. R5 emits complete request, timing, coordinate and trajectory records; the old unequal-batch cohort is rejected.

Packed-multi-token capture classification excludes BF16/F16, so that selector omitted the production projection dispatch in both gate arms. The initial missing-instrument-feature explanation is retracted: instrumentation was already transitively enabled. C7 uses all nodes at step zero and joins request brackets, bound extents, actual dispatch records and hashed MSL. Node116 BF16 projection is scalar reduction with the gate off and simdgroup matrix multiplication with it on. Other F32 tiled operations exist in both arms; generic matrix-instruction presence is insufficient attribution.

HF forward variants reuse one immutable Arc<ModelWeights> through with_forward_descriptor; each graph retains separate logical KV and cache identity. Last payload destruction owns resident cleanup; rejected strong_count polling, clearing resident caches and reloading weights per arm. The live four-arm process completes its retained-arm cohort after an earlier same-name/different-pointer ResidentNameRebound. Native fixtures retain pointers, owned/packed bytes, survivor outputs, typed rejection and final empty census. CPU concurrent destruction does not claim cross-thread Metal cleanup.

Frozen shared-owner Metal candidate and independent native F32 references are compared for both synthetic prefixes across baseline, fixed logits, adaptive logits and fixed hidden. Full coordinate differences in both directions, scalar comparisons, ID/byte selections and wrong-prefix rejection are retained. Non-exact coordinates remain non-exact despite satisfying the admitted bound; this is not BF16 activation bit reproduction or a general quality evaluation. Adaptive host metadata and device strength originate in separate reductions; their numerical difference has a targeted diagnostic investigation.

Identical saved C2 logits replayed through the production adaptive partition reproduce both original Metal strength-only scalars exactly; requesting all intermediate outputs changes Metal strength. Captured denominator-plus-division MSL uses stride-256 lane sums, simd_sum and partial-group merge, whereas the materialized denominator uses a serial fold. reduce_is_cooperative_dispatch admits broadcast epilogues without TreeReduce admission although NumericPolicy withholds reassociation. This is a shared lowering permission bypass, not an Ouro formula change. Registered C2 tolerance acceptance did not establish numeric-policy compliance; original artifacts remain source-condition evidence and the repair receives a separate spec/checkpoint.

Owner proposes favoring decode streams with available KV using expected residency or Bloom screening. Existing BlockBloom and PromptCache::bloom_candidates screen token-block content within matching CacheKey entries and currently feed telemetry; PrefixTrie verifies exact prefix token IDs. Proposed scheduler reuses exact active-stream ownership/residency first and screens larger inventories with Bloom only when useful. Positive membership never authorizes KV reuse: context/position, model/configuration, logical layer/visit and allocation validity must match. Preserve bounded aging/prefill service; compare fixed arrival workloads with per-selection payloads, transfers, latency, throughput and repeated-run CoV before claiming benefit. Existing bloom_candidates scans and allocates, so it is not a ready-made zero-allocation scheduler.

Proposed investigation beyond reuse: decode-shape kernels and byte traffic, compatible multi-stream batching with bounded prefills, permitted fusion, lower host encoding/readback boundaries, overlap, target-verified speculation, separately admitted precision/storage changes and expert-grouped MoE execution. Existing placement path already retains non-root placed outputs and supports chunking; root readback and host logits sampling remain source boundaries. Existing cached attention fusion/plan reuse must be audited for coverage, not reintroduced. Prioritize elapsed critical-path evidence, preserve target semantics and report complete paired request/token payloads plus CoV; hardware utilization alone is not the objective. No new acceleration measurement is claimed.

The shared Metal generic broadcast epilogue uses the original ordered fold when TreeReduce is denied and retains cooperative output writes. Actual replay MSL captures lane-zero ordered accumulation. Executed emitter/specialization/device assertions, saved-input controls, strict live requests, relaxed cached generation and fresh independent C2 comparisons are indexed with raw payloads, source brackets and failures. Complete signed coordinates remain non-exact against the independent reference; registered bounds are not bit equality. Strict live timing means increased across retained cells; relaxed cached timing differences are not attributed to the branch. Multi-stream scheduling and additional acceleration levers remain explicitly unmeasured proposals.

Owner requires parallelization and performance strategies to be Proxima knobs/integrations under the unified programmable interface. Existing Omega RuntimeConfig has Settings/serde/builder, but serving dispatch/chunk controls remain Metal-specific; multi-sequence/phase interleaving are rejected and overlap_transfer_compute documents an unwired arm. Extend existing serving, planner and backend owners under one composed policy rather than adding disconnected booleans or another executor. Distinguish kernel, DAG, request, overlap and device parallelism; preserve token/refinement dependencies. Resource budgets and semantic permissions constrain measured backend candidate selection. Required unsupported behavior rejects and effective choices must be observable. Implementation/performance benefit of this full contract is unmeasured.

Owner requested a restart prompt to clear the session and finish the unified programmable interface including parallelization. RESTART-PROMPT.md preserves current implemented evidence, source gaps, full integration objective, detailed worker-packet requirements, native-command-only restriction, per-checkpoint real-model E2E, llama performance oracle and CoV/payload discipline. This is a handoff instruction, not evidence that the expanded integration has been implemented.

Round-one plan tournament selected a memory-first integration boundary: preserve checkpoint9, prepare the allocation ledger and runner, then integrate mapped-weight windows, bounded dense binding/output/Plan slots, KV, routed experts and transition/cache ownership as one boundary before policy, continuation, scheduler or strategy work. Three judges ranked the synthesis first (Borda 6 versus 3 and 0); round two is in progress. This is an execution order proposal, not an implementation result.

Qwen3-1.7B-BF16 source-capture checkpoint9 was partial and was terminated after macOS vmmap reported physical footprint 2.6G with peak 4.8G. Four Qwen Proxima cohort/request rows were retained; Granite MoE had not started and llama had zero cohort rows, so the checkpoint is not a dense/MoE/oracle comparison. The mapped GGUF, output product and allocation region payloads are retained; MALLOC_LARGE and graphics VM range ownership remains unresolved without pointer joins. A corrected source audit found existing per-layer checkpoint and routed expert discard callers; this does not prove cap-compliant residency.

The embedding binder accepts row-decodable F16/BF16 blocks into BoundWeights::packed and a literal BF16 test observes borrowed source bytes with no owned F32 tensor. Qwen3 checkpoint17 records native footprint 58,336,832 current and 63,104,576 lifetime peak bytes at model-load completion under a 500,000,000-byte cap; its later generation attempt fails before dispatch at ArenaOverCap. Qwen3 checkpoint18 reports peak_bytes=1,246,414,464, cap_bytes=864,060,625, query_rows=5; Granite 3.1 MoE reports peak_bytes=201,634,008, cap_bytes=172,812,125, query_rows=1. The arena source now computes the live output peak and returns the typed cap error before calling allocate_buffer. The C9 plan source ties Qwen's high live output to node3192 extents [1,2048,151936] before node3193's vocabulary reduction. Neither checkpoint generated tokens or produced llama.cpp comparison rows. The bounded Qwen output projection, Granite MoE live-set integration, and AC18 lifecycle ledger remain unimplemented.

CP24 Qwen mixed_three_stream, paired Proxima/llama.cpp, retains 16 request comparisons across two samples. In both samples unified stream41 differs at output token positions 40-63 and stream89 at 20,53,56; stream73 matches. The other 10 serial and single-workload rows match. Every row has matched input_ids, 64 output tokens and no EOS. This is observed output behavior only; dispatch-to-kernel-source ownership is not joined, and the cached-length mechanism is not established.

The composed two-range Mistral binding regression observes stream0 output NodeId(86) using cached_len NodeId(15) as operand nine and stream1 output NodeId(207) using NodeId(136). The runtime cached_len nodes are absent from arithmetic ancestry. Renaming only stream1 cached_len declines its fusion, leaves stream0 bound to NodeId(15), and does not use unnamespaced decoy NodeId(1). This proves the focused matcher behavior on that fixture; CP24 real-model causality remains unestablished pending paired CP25 payload and dispatch/source joins.

CP25 Qwen3-1.7B BF16 mixed_three_stream paired run used the pinned model digest ef2864916b951ebd2f072c759d11a442ba31acc3bcb7e5db5ca1d6fcf78b93cb, three arrival-ordered streams 41/73/89, 64 output tokens/request, bit_exact numeric policy, Metal, and one non-warmup sample per arm. All 12 request input-ID arrays and output-ID arrays match between Proxima and llama.cpp; output arrays total 768 tokens per runtime and every per-request difference array is empty. CP24 had four mismatching unified requests on streams 41/89 across two samples; CP25 outputs for those streams changed from the CP24 Proxima sequences and match the CP25 llama.cpp sequences. The one source change between checkpoints was candidate-scoped cached_len binding, but the actual failing dispatch-to-pipeline-source association is absent because the runner records source plans only after the cohort and plan caches are replaced. Thus the real-model causal mechanism is plausible, not proven. Performance measurements for the one non-warmup sample are cohort_response_ms: Proxima serial 144063.390833, Proxima unified 139808.109959, llama.cpp serial 1153.484584, llama.cpp unified 993.016834; cohort conditions are same model/workload/input set, three streams, 64-token outputs, one measured sample. CoV is unmeasured. The physical-footprint file records startup and model_load_complete only; the lifecycle cap remains unmeasured.

CP25 Granite 3.1 1B A400M MoE mixed_three_stream used artifact digest cd60b3e8bb445d4c05e0b0b99b1bb41e8bb77211b161e783c71931168131df80, architecture granitemoe, 32 experts and 8 experts per token. Across 12 paired requests, input IDs match while all output IDs differ; outputs have 64 IDs/request and do not end in EOS. Complete arrays and position deltas are retained. The observed differences also occur in serial rows, so the payload does not isolate scheduling; their token mechanism is unexplained. The one measured sample reports Proxima serial/unified cohort_response_ms 135599.811833/151026.135959 and llama.cpp serial/unified 1387.416209/1163.885417; CoV is unmeasured. Full-run physical-footprint attribution remains unmeasured: only startup and model_load_complete snapshots exist; their lifetime peaks are 2376576 and 47845632 bytes, respectively.

CP25 Granite serial and unified Proxima runs produce the same four complete output sequences per stream; each sequence differs from the matching llama.cpp sequence starting at token one. The checkpoint GGUF stores attention.scale=0.015625, embedding_scale=12, residual_scale≈0.22 and logit_scale=6 at payload offsets 0x536, 0x560, 0x589 and 0x5af. Proxima architecture_from_metadata omits them and the generic Mistral descriptor emits inverse-sqrt attention scaling (0.125 for head dimension 64); llama.cpp Granite graph reads and applies all four. This is an observed source/data discrepancy and a plausible explanation, not an established cause. A separate tied-router-score hypothesis is visible in the emitted router source, but no route-score payload establishes a tie. Next: capture first-prefix intermediate/route/logit payloads and exact source, then toggle one metadata scale at a time.

CP26 Qwen3-1.7B BF16 digest ef2864916b951ebd2f072c759d11a442ba31acc3bcb7e5db5ca1d6fcf78b93cb, mixed_three_stream, streams 41/73/89, Metal, bit_exact, one measured sample per serial/unified arm and 64 output IDs/request. All 12 input arrays and all 12 output arrays match paired llama.cpp: 768 IDs per runtime, zero differing positions (exact token-ID evidence, not full logits). Per Proxima execution source capture retained 800 dispatch rows and 800 execution references, joined to 17 unique plan-source rows with zero unjoined references. Measured cohort_response_ms: Proxima serial/unified 120100.004292/127159.77925; llama.cpp serial/unified 1003.814708/995.3365 under the stated same model/workload/sample conditions. CoV is unmeasured. CP25 Proxima values 144063.390833/139808.109959 are retained under a different instrumentation condition; no timing cause or comparison conclusion is established. Only startup and model_load_complete physical-footprint snapshots exist; lifecycle-cap status remains unmeasured.

CP26 Granite 3.1 1B A400M MoE digest cd60b3e8bb445d4c05e0b0b99b1bb41e8bb77211b161e783c71931168131df80, mixed_three_stream, streams 41/73/89, Metal, bit_exact, one measured sample per serial/unified arm and 64 output IDs/request. All 12 input arrays match llama.cpp; none of the 12 output arrays match. Across 768 positions, 764 IDs differ; first tokens are 26/34/2953 in Proxima and 203/48841/14084 in llama.cpp for streams 41/73/89. Each stream's Proxima sequence is repeated across serial/unified and warmup/measured, so the token payload does not isolate batching. Per Proxima execution source capture retained 804 dispatch rows/references, joined to 16 unique plan-source rows with zero unjoined references. Measured cohort_response_ms: Proxima serial/unified 104066.449667/113838.108083; llama.cpp serial/unified 798.290625/910.667208 under the same model/workload/sample conditions. CoV is unmeasured. Only startup and model_load_complete physical-footprint snapshots exist, so the full-run lifecycle cap remains unmeasured. The actual cause of first-token differences remains unexplained pending aligned intermediate/router/logit payloads and a single-scale toggle.

CP27 Qwen Proxima and llama.cpp payloads completed, but final sampler status rejected physical-footprint capture after cadence deadline and native current/ledger-peak inconsistencies. CP28 was manually interrupted before llama.cpp after RSS and Metal allocation counters exceeded the requested byte ceiling while native samples were inconsistent. Those distinct counters prove neither cap breach nor pass. AC18 allocation admission, owner joins and fence lifetime remain open. Next adapt mapping, bound-weight, Plan, KV, expert, cache and fence owners to one reservation boundary and rerun exact Qwen/Granite payloads before another source integration.
